candidates.statement: This implies that the low-lying Dirac eigenvalues must be spaced like $\sim 1/V$.

Based on an analysis of sum rules derived by Leutwyler and Smilga \cite{Leut92} for the inverse powers of the Dirac eigenvalues in a finite volume, Shuryak and Verbaarschot conjectured that the microscopic spectral density should be a universal quantity which depends only on global symmetries, the number of flavors $N_f$, and the topological charge $\nu$.

Here we proceed as follows: Since the polynomial $p_n^{(N_f)}(x,M)$ has to be invariant under permutations of the masses $M_f$ and must have a finite limit when all quark masses are degenerate, a reasonable guess for the normalization function is \begin{eqnarray} C_n^{(N_f)}(M) \ = \ \det\left[L_{n+f-1}^{(0)} (-N\Sigma^2M_{f^\prime}^2)\right]_{f,f^\prime=1,\ldots,N_f}\:, \label{polnorm} \end{eqnarray} see Sec.~\ref{sec23} below, in particular Eq.~(\ref{chefformel}).
In the limit $m_f\to 0$, our results must reduce to those obtained earlier in the chiral limit \cite{Verb93}.
The RMT result should be universal and identical with that of full QCD under the same conditions as the microscopic spectral density.
The factor $c_N^{(N_f)}(m)$ ensures that $E(0,0)=1$ and should not be confused with the normalization constant defined in Eqs.~(\ref{polnorm}) and (\ref{CNfm}).
